title: Changes That Never Clash — Libraries That Agree in the End
description: Conflict-free replicated data types told in the compendium of the scholars' coast: an entry made of parts, each merged by its own rule, from a count of comet sightings kept in pebbles with a column for each library to cross-references and headings with a tag for every writing, and what such parts can and cannot keep.
question: Can some changes be combined in any order, any number of times, and still come out the same everywhere, so that they never clash and no one ever needs to coordinate?
how: We find out by exploring how the libraries of the scholars' coast keep one compendium of knowledge, each changing its own copy at once and merging the copies the couriers bring, without ever meeting to settle anything.
credit: Shapiro, Preguiça, Baquero & Zawirski 2011 · the same authors' comprehensive study, 2011

papers.authors: Marc Shapiro, Nuno Preguiça, Carlos Baquero and Marek Zawirski
